chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the deceased dies, Allah sends an angel to the most pained one of his family, and he wipes upon his heart, causing him to forget the anguish of grief; and had it not for that, the world would not be inhabited (by people living through the grief).'

key_terms.أَوْجَعِ أَهْلِهِ: the most pained/grieving of his family
key_terms.فَمَسَحَ عَلَى قَلْبِهِ: and he wiped upon his heart

ai.seo_question: How does Allah comfort the grieving family of the deceased according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni narrates that an angel visits the most grief-stricken family member to wipe away the overwhelming pain of loss, a divine mercy cited as essential for humanity's continued existence in the world. This mechanism highlights the Shia understanding of *law'at al-huzn* not merely as emotional distress, but as a physiological and spiritual burden that, if unmitigated, would hinder human endurance and societal continuity.
